Athletic Association men's basketball season|2015]]) }} '''Elijah Brigham Bryant''' (born April 19, 1995) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] and the [[EuroLeague]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon Phoenix]] and [[BYU Cougars men's basketball|Brigham Young Cougars]]. He has played on teams that have been [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]] champion ([[2019–20 Israeli Basketball Premier League|2020]]), [[List of NBA champions|NBA champion]] ([[2021 NBA Finals|2021]]), [[EuroLeague]] champion ([[2021-22 EuroLeague|2022]]), and [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]] champion ([[2022-23 Basketbol Süper Ligi|2023]]). ==Early life== Born in [[Gwinnett County, Georgia]],{{cite web|title=Elijah Bryant Player Profile|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/player/Bryant-Elijah/USA/Maccabi-T-A/336386|work=Eurobasket.com|access-date=August 31, 2018}} Bryant began playing basketball at a young age, always playing against older children. As a junior in high school, he had a growth spurt and grew one foot in a year. He attended [[New Hampton School]] in [[New Hampton, New Hampshire]], where he averaged 13 points, four rebounds, and four assists per game and led the Huskies to the [[New England Preparatory School Athletic Council|NEPSAC]] AAA final.{{cite news|title=Elijah Bryant Profile – BYU Athletics|url=https://byucougars.com/athlete/m-basketball/112561/Elijah-Bryant|work=BYUCougars.com|accessdate=August 31, 2018}} ==College career== [[File:Elijah Bryant.jpg|thumb|260px|Bryant as a college freshman in 2015]] Bryant started his college career with [[Elon Phoenix men's basketball|Elon University]], with whom he averaged 14.2 points (8th in the league), 4.2 rebounds, 2.7 assists, and 1.3 steals (10th) per game in his freshman year. Bryant was named [[Colonial Athletic Association]] (CAA) Rookie of the Year and earned spots on the Third-team All-CAA and the CAA All-Rookie Team.{{cite news|url=http://www.caasports.com/news/2015/3/5/MBB_0305154313.aspx|title=W&M's Thornton Headlines All-CAA Men's Basketball Team|date=March 5, 2015|work=CAASports.com|access-date=August 31, 2018}} On July 28, 2015, Bryant transferred from Elon to [[Brigham Young University]] (BYU), but he sat out first season at BYU per NCAA transfer rules.{{cite news|title=Guard Elijah Bryant announces he is transferring to BYU|url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/865633415/Guard-Elijah-Bryant-announces-he-is-transferring-to-BYU.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150729150628/http://www.deseretnews.com/article/865633415/Guard-Elijah-Bryant-announces-he-is-transferring-to-BYU.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 29, 2015|date=July 28, 2015|work=DeseretNews.com|access-date=August 31, 2018}} He posted 11.7 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 2.2 assists per game as a sophomore in 2016-17. He only played in 23 games, due to a knee injury.{{cite news|last1=Drew|first1=Jay|url=https://www.sltrib.com/sports/2017/11/08/elijah-bryant-luke-worthington-are-byu-basketball-captains-for-2017-18-season/|title=Elijah Bryant, Luke Worthington are BYU basketball captains for 2017-18 season|work=[[The Salt Lake Tribune]]|date=November 8, 2017|accessdate=August 31, 2018}} Despite his injury, Bryant scored a career-high 39 points, including seven 3-pointers, in a win against [[Portland Pilots men's basketball|Portland]].{{cite news|last1=Call|first1=Jeff|title=How Elijah Brigham Bryant overcame knee injuries to star for BYU|url=https://www.deseretnews.com/article/865696175/How-Elijah-Brigham-Bryant-overcame-knee-injuries-to-star-for-BYU.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180222052852/https://www.deseretnews.com/article/865696175/How-Elijah-Brigham-Bryant-overcame-knee-injuries-to-star-for-BYU.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 22, 2018|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=February 21, 2018|accessdate=August 31, 2018}} In his junior year at BYU in 2017-18, Bryant finished the season as the [[West Coast Conference]] (WCC) second-leading scorer with 18.1 points per game, third in free-throw percentage (.850), third in 3-point field goal percentage (.415), fourth in steals (1.3), eighth in rebounds (6.3), and tied for seventh in double-doubles. On February 27, 2018, Bryant earned a spot in the First-team All-WCC.{{cite news|title=BYU Men's Hoops: Bryant, Haws, Childs earn All-WCC honors|url=https://www.heraldextra.com/sports/college/byu/basketball/men/byu-men-s-hoops-bryant-haws-childs-earn-all-wcc/article_6cc758f1-9c21-5c05-88b2-eb7984dced55.html|date=February 27, 2018|work=HeraldExtra.com|access-date=August 31, 2018}}{{Dead link|date=March 2024 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} On April 18, 2018, after completing his junior year at BYU, Bryant announced his plans to graduate and forgo his remaining eligibility for a professional career.{{cite news|title=BYU star Elijah Bryant announces plans to graduate, turn pro|url=https://www.ksl.com/article/46302846/byu-star-elijah-bryant-announces-plans-to-graduate-turn-pro|date=April 18, 2018|work=KSL.com|access-date=August 31, 2018}} ==Professional career== ===Hapoel Eilat (2018–2019)=== After going undrafted in the [[2018 NBA draft]], Bryant joined the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] for the [[2018 NBA Summer League]].{{cite news|title=Summer 76 – Summer League Roster Finalized|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/summer-76-summer-league-roster-finalized|date=July 5, 2018|work=NBA.com|accessdate=August 31, 2018}} On August 30, 2018, Bryant started his professional career with [[Hapoel Eilat B.C.|Hapoel Eilat]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]], signing a one-year deal.{{cite news|url=http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/287098/hapoel-eilat-signs-rookie-elijah-bryant.html|title=Hapoel Eilat signs rookie Elijah Bryant|date=August 30, 2018|work=Sportando.basketball|accessdate=August 31, 2018|archive-date=May 12, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190512213447/http://archive.sportando.basketball/en/europe/israel/287098/hapoel-eilat-signs-rookie-elijah-bryant.html|url-status=dead}} On October 29, 2018, he recorded a season-high 31 points, shooting 11-of-20 from the field, along with seven rebounds in an 81–75 win over [[Bnei Herzliya]].{{cite news|title=Winner League, Game 4: Hapoel Eilat Vs Herzliya|url=http://basket.co.il/game-zone.asp?GameId=23809&lang=en|work=basket.co.il|date=October 29, 2018|access-date=May 13, 2019}} On December 4, 2018, Bryant was named [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Player of the Month|Israeli Basketball Premier League Player of the Month]] after averaging 20.5 points, 8.3 rebounds, and 2 steals in four games played in November.{{cite news|title=שחקן חודש נובמבר: אלייז'ה בראיינט|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=19608|work=basket.co.il|date=December 4, 2018|access-date=December 4, 2018|language=he}} He helped Eilat reach the [[2019 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four]], where they eventually lost to [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]]. In 36 games played for Eilat, he finished as the [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#Statistical leaders|league]] 's fourth-leading scorer (17.5 points per game) and fourth in [[Performance Index Rating|efficiency rating]] (19.4 per game), along with 5.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, and 1.4 steals per game, as he shot .558 from the field.[https://basketball.realgm.com/player/Elijah-Bryant/Summary/80581 "Elijah Bryant"], realgm.com. On June 6, 2019, Bryant earned a spot on the [[2018–19 Israeli Basketball Premier League#All-Israeli League Teams|All-Israeli Basketball Premier League First Team]].{{cite news|title=מצטייני עונת 2018/19 בליגת ווינר סל|url=http://basket.co.il/news.asp?id=21288|work=basket.co.il|date=June 6, 2019|access-date=July 6, 2019|language=he}} ===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2019–2021)=== On July 1, 2019, Bryant joined the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] for the [[2019 NBA Summer League]], where he averaged 14.2 points, 4.0 rebounds, and 3.2 assists per game.{{cite news|title=Bucks Announce Roster for MGM Resorts NBA Summer League 2019|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-announce-roster-mgm-resorts-nba-summer-league-2019|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2019|access-date=July 6, 2019}} In 49 games for Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2019-20, he averaged 8.9 points, 3.6 rebounds, 2.1 assists, and 1.1 steals per game. On July 23, 2019, Bryant signed a two-year deal with [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]].{{cite news|title=Maccabi brings aboard swingman Bryant|url=https://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9tixjaticxvjgqas/maccabi-brings-aboard-swingman-bryant|work=EuroLeague.net|date=July 23, 2019|access-date=July 23, 2019}} On February 5, 2020, Bryant recorded a [[EuroLeague]] career-high 21 points, while shooting 9-of-19 from the field, along with six rebounds and four assists, leading Maccabi to an 80–77 win over [[BC Khimki|Khimki]].{{cite news|title=Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv vs. Khimki Moscow Region - Game|url=https://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=206&seasoncode=E2019|work=EuroLeague.net|date=February 5, 2020|access-date=February 7, 2020}} In 52 games for Maccabi Tel Aviv in 2020-21, he averaged 11.1 points, 3.3 rebounds, 2.2 assists, and 0.8 steals per game, shooting .840 from the free throw line. On May 10, 2021, he left Maccabi Tel Aviv.{{cite news|title=Maccabi Tel Aviv officially allows Elijah Bryant to pursue his NBA dream|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/maccabi-tel-aviv-officially-allows-elijah-bryant-to-pursue-his-nba-dream/|work=Sportando.basketball|date=May 10, 2021|access-date=May 10, 2021}} === Milwaukee Bucks (2021) === On May 13, 2021, Bryant signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite news|title=Bucks Sign Elijah Bryant|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-elijah-bryant|work=NBA.com|date=May 13, 2021|access-date=May 15, 2021}} In his first and only regular-season NBA game, Bryant scored 16 points against the [[Chicago Bulls]] on May 16, 2021, in the Bucks' season finale. He won an [[NBA championship]] when the Bucks defeated the [[Phoenix Suns]] in 6 games in the [[2021 NBA Finals]]. By playing 11 playoff games and only one regular season game in his NBA career, Bryant has played in 10 more playoffs games in his career than he has regular season games.{{Cite web|title=Elijah Bryant Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/bryanel01.html|access-date=2022-02-11|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}} In those 11 playoff games he averaged 1.3 points and 1.1 rebounds in 4.5 minutes per game. On September 26, he was waived by the Bucks, but he was re-signed three days later.{{cite web|last1=Shaw|first1=JD|title=Bucks Waive Elijah Bryant|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/09/bucks-waive-elijah-bryant.html|website=Hoops Rumors|date=September 26, 2021|access-date=September 26, 2021}}{{cite web|title=Bucks Sign Elijah Bryant and Johnny O'Bryant|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-elijah-bryant-and-johnny-obryant|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2021|access-date=September 29, 2021}} On October 14, the Bucks again waived Bryant.{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Request Waivers on Elijah Bryant|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-request-waivers-elijah-bryant|website=NBA.com|date=October 14, 2021|access-date=October 16, 2021}} === Anadolu Efes (2021–2025) === On October 18, 2021, Bryant signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the [[Basketball Super League|Basketbol Süper Ligi]] in [[Turkey]].{{cite web|title=Amerikalı oyuncu Elijah Bryant ile iki yıllık sözleşme imzaladık|url=https://www.anadoluefessk.org/haber/elijah-bryant-anadolu-efes-te|website=AnadoluEfesSK.org|date=October 18, 2021|access-date=October 18, 2021|language=tr}} On May 21, 2022, Bryant won the Euroleague with Anadolu Efes, grabbing 8 rebounds and contributing one assist in the championship game win against Real Madrid. On June 22, 2023, it was announced that he had renewed his contract for another two years. On October 15, 2024, Bryant was suspended for Round 3 of the 2024-2025 Turkish Airlines EuroLeague regular season. He was also fined 10,000 [[euros]].{{cite web |title=Elijah Bryant and Tarik Biberovic to serve suspensions in Round 3 |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1728369/elijah-bryant-and-tarik-biberovic-to-serve-suspensions-in-round-3-euroleague/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=15 October 2024 |language=en |date=15 October 2024}} Bryant had gotten into a scuffle under the basket with [[Tarik Biberovic]]. Referees had to intervene and break them apart, ultimately resulting in both of them being ejected and both were suspended for one match.{{cite web |title=Biberovic and Bryant suspended after Istanbul derby incident, Efes and Fenerbahce will appeal |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/euroleague/1728095/biberovic-and-bryant-suspended-after-istanbul-derby-incident-anadolu-efes-and-fenerbahce-will-appeal/ |website=Eurohoops |access-date=15 October 2024 |language=en |date=14 October 2024}} On July 1, 2025, Bryant parted ways with the Turkish team.{{cite web |title=Anadolu Efes, Elijah Bryant officially part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/anadolu-efes-elijah-bryant-officially-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 1, 2025 |date=July 1, 2025}} === Hapoel Tel Aviv (2025–present) === On July 6, 2025, Bryant signed with [[Hapoel Tel Aviv B.C.|Hapoel Tel Aviv]] of the [[Israeli Basketball Premier League]].{{Cite web|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/elijah-bryant-signs-multi-year-deal-with-hapoel-tel-aviv/|title=Elijah Bryant signs multi-year deal with Hapoel Tel Aviv|last=|first=|date=July 6, 2025|website=|publisher=Sportando|language=En|access-date=July 6, 2025}} In 52 games for Hapoel Tel Aviv in 2025-26, he averaged 15.0 points, 5.0 rebounds, 3.7 assists, and 0.7 steals per game, while shooting .512 from the field and .854 from the free throw line. On July 11, 2026, the team extended Bryant's contract until 2029.{{cite web |title=Hapoel Tel Aviv extend their star guard |url=https://basketnews.com/news-251829-hapoel-tel-aviv-extend-their-star-guard.html |website=basketnews.com |access-date=14 July 2026 |language=en}} ==Career statistics== {{Euroleague player statistics legend}} ===NBA=== ====Regular season==== {| class="wikitable" |- | style="background:#AFE6BA; colspan="2"| Career | 91 || 56 || 28.8 || .437 || .366 || .800 || 4.9 || 2.4 || 1.2 || .4 || 15.1 {{S-end}} ==Personal life== Bryant is the son of Israel Bryant and Reginald Strother, a physician. He is a member of the [[Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints]] (the Mormon Church). Bryant remarked in 2020, after playing in Israel, "“I’ve come to respect the Jews a lot because they’re very similar to Mormons. They value family.
